summary.intent: Evaluate and flesh out SEED-001: whether the production Phala TEE CVM can be power-cycled on-demand (stop/start between cron runs) to eliminate always-on compute costs given its <1% duty cycle.
summary.outcome: A 5-agent parallel workflow produced a full feasibility brief. SEED-001 was enriched with architecture options, cost model, key-continuity analysis, and a sequenced recommendation. The file is modified but uncommitted, status set to dormant with clear next spikes defined.

repo: The TEE worker is a persistent Express server with no internal scheduler — it is woken exclusively by the API's BullMQ cron POSTing /republish on a `0 */6 * * *` schedule (4 runs/day).
IPNS records carry a 48h EOL but are republished every 6h, giving an 8× safety margin — even a 25-min cold-start is trivially safe against the freshness deadline.
TEE keys are deterministically derived per epoch via `DstackClient.getKey('cipherbox/ipns-republish', 'epoch-${N}')` bound to the CVM app_id — no private key is persisted in the worker.

stop/start preserves app_id and therefore re-derives identical epoch keys (safe); destroy/recreate that yields a new app_id permanently bricks all ECIES-wrapped IPNS keys — documented as a CRITICAL rule in docker-compose.phala.yml and 35-RESEARCH.md.

There is zero attestation/quote verification anywhere in the codebase (repo-wide grep for getQuote|attestation|dcap|RA-TLS returns zero hits) — clients trust teePublicKey as served by the API, so quote instability across boots is a non-issue today.
The production CVM identity is ambiguous: the compose is named `cipherbox-tee-staging` with CIPHERBOX_ENVIRONMENT=staging, so it is unclear whether this is truly prod or a separate prod CVM exists.
Phala GPU TEE CVMs have a 24h billing minimum per launch — on-demand cycling is only economical for CPU/TDX CVMs, which our worker uses.

code.finding: Contains an inline CRITICAL rule: never destroy+recreate into a new app_id, as this bricks all ECIES-wrapped IPNS keys permanently.
Also documents the key-bricking warning for destroy/recreate of the TEE CVM.

Enriched with full decision-ready brief: key-continuity analysis, cost model (~85-95% compute reduction but likely single-digit $/mo absolute), 4 architecture options, recommendation sequence, and 6 open spikes.

workflow: Used a 5-agent parallel workflow (fan-out over 4 subsystems + synthesis) to simultaneously investigate republish cadence, TEE key lifecycle, deployment topology, and Phala lifecycle API before synthesizing a decision brief.
Phala bills per-second with no monthly minimum for CPU/TDX CVMs; a stopped CVM halts compute charges but still bills storage (~$0.10/GB/mo); only DELETE eliminates storage cost entirely.
Cold-start duration is image-size-dominated: small image ~1-2 min, large image (e.g. 1.4GB) ~20-25 min — this determines the savings ceiling more than execution time.

The zero-risk first step before any orchestration work is to downsize the always-on CVM (e.g. from medium to small), which captures a large fraction of savings with no key risk and no new failure modes.

friction: Key continuity across stop/start is theoretically sound from dstack KMS docs but has not been empirically verified against the actual production app — it remains an unconfirmed assumption.
Exact CVM size, disk footprint, and image tag are not pinned in the repo (image tag may be `latest`), making the cost model estimates rather than hard numbers.
Cold-start time is unknown without measurement — determines whether savings are meaningful or eroded by long boot windows.
Production vs staging CVM identity is unresolved: cannot safely orchestrate stop/start without first confirming which CVM is actually production.
open_items: Key-continuity spike (blocking): on a throwaway TDX CVM, derive getKey() for an epoch → phala cvms stop → start → re-derive → assert identical teePublicKey (~30 min).
Cold-start measurement: time `phala cvms start` → /health ready for the actual image; confirm whether start re-pulls layers (~30 min).
Resolve prod-vs-staging CVM identity via `phala cvms list` to know which CVM would actually be cycled.
Pull `phala cvms get <app_id>` for prod to get real size/disk GB/image tag and convert cost estimates to actual numbers (~10 min).
Downsize always-on CVM to `small` if not already — zero-risk first step to capture savings before any orchestration work.
If spikes pass, implement Option A (stop/start same CVM): extend API cron to start → poll /health → republish → stop, and provision Phala API creds (none exist in CI today).
SEED-001 file is a working-tree change (uncommitted) — needs to be folded into the next planning commit.
